title: Degree Barrier for Global Rollout Contrasts on Random Regular Graphs via Two-Sided Exposure Capacity
banked_reason: Sound inherited capacity/GATE mathematics is repository-subsumed; four produced angles and one root revision exhausted all credible field-tier alternatives without a qualifying distinct kernel.
gap_reasons: The actual random-regular balanced two-arm capacity scale and its full-GATE lower-barrier transfer duplicate the central kernel of failed bank run exp_randomregular_fullgate_minimax_frontier; replacing its withdrawn switching route with pairing exposure is not, by itself, a new research-question kernel.

No qualifying growing-radius transition was established. The available small-radius argument substitutes degree powers into inherited bounds; the saturation argument reuses archived observability and correlated-block mechanisms. A new collision-dependent theorem with distinct conclusions across a critical radius remains uncertified.
proof_attempt_summary: Four produced angles and one root revision were attempted: capacity/GATE, accepted-reservoir covariance, correlated endpoint blocks, and growing exposure radius. The initial kernel was repository-subsumed; the later routes reproduced archived mechanisms or failed to establish the needed distinct theorem. The terminal consultation confirmed proposal exhaustion at the mandatory field floor; informal supporting mathematics and finite checks are retained, with no D0 derivation or Lean formalization undertaken and no achieved novelty tier independently calibrated.
tldr: A global rollout contrast requires information about two incompatible endpoint arms. A legal fixed-schedule prior converts the smaller observable arm into the universal lower bound \([12\{b_2(G)+2\}]^{-1}\). The research kernel is a capacity theorem for the actual square of a uniform labelled simple regular graph when \(d\to\infty\) and \(d\le n^{1/8}\): balanced opposite-arm capacity has order \(n\log d/d^2\), with a quantitative tail and a finite lower witness. Certification would sharpen the published global-risk lower edge from \(d/n\) to \(d^2/(n\log d)\), retaining the credited \(d^2/n\) upper edge. On a common complete bounded ANI class, global risk exceeds direct risk by at least order \(d/\log d\). The statistical logarithm remains unresolved.
gap: Kandiros, Harshaw, and Sävje, Corollary 5.4, leaves a polynomial degree gap for the global causal contrast. Ordinary-graph bi-holes and the largest independent set of the exposure conflict graph do not measure the smaller opposite-arm endpoint sample.
fill: A two-stage exposure argument for labelled stubs, a classical lower-witness construction with finite thresholds, and a credited conflict-design upper produce an honest risk interval. The prospective consumer is a rollout comparison of the kind studied in the LinkedIn feed experiments of Saveski and colleagues; random regularity and ANI are maintained theoretical contracts, not empirical assertions.
